text: A pull request starts the gate. The checkout includes the merge commit and its first parent. The command compares those revisions, so the change list describes this pull request. The runner gives the changed paths to the selector. An English shipment edit adds that notice identifier to the affected set. The catalog then supplies its English, French, and German variants. A French only edit selects one file. Changing shared inputs selects the whole catalog instead. This distinction keeps small reviews fast without skipping consumers of a shared definition. Partner notices are separate source identities. They share a contract, but an English shipment text edit does not select the partner text. Keep source dependencies separate from contract dependencies; that distinction matters in the final finding. The runner resolves the English source before comparing any translation. It loads the contract selected by the catalog entry. Missing sources or unreadable contracts become file errors, rather than silently passing. The allowed set combines three sources. Shared inputs provide the brand name and support link. Direct inputs supply the recipient and tracking link. Derived values add the item table, which is built before rendering. All three are allowed in the template. The inspector parses data, not executable template code. It requires a nonempty body, then reads placeholders separately from each field. Repeated names collapse into a set; their order and repetition are not part of this contract. Unknown inputs are reported with their field and source side. Malformed placeholders become document errors. If English is invalid, validation returns immediately; blaming every translation for a broken source would hide the real cause. Once English is valid, the candidate translation is inspected with the same allowed set. A broken document returns its parse error. Otherwise, comparison continues, retaining any unknown input errors already found. Each field is compared independently. Removing the subject produces a field presence issue. Moving the item table from the body into the preview also fails; preserving a name somewhere in the document is not enough. The validator compares the names in both directions. Missing names appear in English but not in the translation. Unexpected names appear in the translation but not in English. Moving the item table into the preview produces one mismatch in each field, even though the contract allows that input. A valid French translation returns no issues. This proves placeholder parity and basic syntax, not translation quality or visual layout. Reordering a sentence or repeating a recipient is permitted; the gate compares sets rather than prose. The runner processes every selected catalog entry. A load failure is attached to that file, and the remaining entries still run. This lets one check report several independent problems instead of stopping at the first exception. The result includes the checked count and every file report. If any file has issues, the exit code is one. The command prints the report and forwards that status to the workflow, so a validation failure blocks the check. A manual audit selects the entire catalog. That full run is useful for investigating a suspicious green pull request check. A zero exit code only describes the selected files; it says nothing about files the selector forgot. Here is a reproduced review finding. Remove the tracking link input from the shipment contract without editing any templates. Five notices still use that input: three language variants, plus two partner overrides. The selector only recognizes template edits and a fixed list of shared files. Contract data paths match neither branch. It returns an empty selection, and the runner reports success after checking zero files. The full audit fails on all five dependents, confirming the validator works. The fix belongs in selection: map changed contracts to every catalog entry using them, including partner overrides. Keep this reproduction as a regression test before calling the gate reliable.
